searchText: Kintsugi testnet is working on stable? I think still lots of forks in there. Just restarted my teku-geth node and this is what teku does on startup. It passes us 15 conflicting heads. We will try to sync all of them and regenerate the state for them. This will horrible break on mainnet where syncing to even one of these heads might take multiple minutes to hours. Note that syncing process on EL side should be fork-specific, i.e. if the canonical chain is in sync and syncing process is happening on even multiple other forks a node should still be fully functioning. Not sure this note is directly related to you recent message, just want to mention it here just in case executePayload is not an indication of the chain head - it’s the blocks we need to validate. forkChoiceUpdated is what tells us the head. The CL *must* call executePayload on every post-merge block it imports as it’s the only way to validate the block hash. In more normal situations we likely only have one chain head but currently on kintsugi there are a ton of forks are we need to try to follow them all. It would be reasonable for the EL to decide to only sync one of those chains at a time btw (probably best to pick the one forkChoiceUpdated is indicating). The others could check the block hash and return SYNCING and the CL will have to retry it later (or a descendant if there are any). At some point though all those chains likely need to be imported unless finalisation invalidates them first. Yeah we need to change how we pick which chain to sync Something in the middle between syncing with everything and with only one chain is to decide to sync with the chain once it's signified by fcU, and still support multiple chain to sync with concurrently Erigon doesn't support multiple chains concurrently. At one point in time there can be only a single current state. A re-org is implemented by reverting state changes from the loser blocks and executing the winner blocks. It does mean that when the head is changed the sync process gets its new target and stops syncing with any other chain, right? The head being ForkchoiceState.headBlockHash, right? We haven't implemented it yet, but that's the idea, yes. To only sync what engine_forkchoiceUpdated tells us and don't sync any other chains. I see, any of these strategies are viable and the final choice is after implementers. Probably, it's really complicated to support multiple syncing processes at a time and doing so doesn't benefit that much. The process of syncing with only a single chain that changes over time should eventually converge despite of the number and frequency of the switching I'm going to start wiping some kintsugi nodes and try to get them all on the same fork. I think we've addressed/have ideas for most of the bugs we encountered. I've stored the databases of quite a few nodes and taken some snapshots, Additionally some protoarrays of random lighthouse nodes. Incase someone would prefer the testnet be in its current state for longer to debug any error, lemme know ASAP. I came here to say what everyone else said 😅 This highlights the dangers of just using executePayload as a signal if there is deep work to do. fcu ftw Is there some aggregated list of what CL clients changed/need to change? This sounds like it’s going to be a problem to me. There are multiple chains because forks happen and you need to be able to process blocks on all forks in order to a) validate them and b) process attestations for them which lets you decide which fork is canonical. Most forks are only one or two blocks long so Erigon could probably reorg, process the block and reorg back (as long as the json rpc requests in the mean time are delayed so they don’t report from the wrong fork), but during non finality forks can be hundreds of blocks long or more and we still need to be able to process blocks from both sides. Otherwise any network split becomes irreversible. <dannyryan> You *must* be able to use heuristics to decide if something is worth processing (akin to if a block had some silly low pow). Or do you have some stronger signal to execute (e.g. some minimal fork choice weight) Which generator was used to prepare genesis state file? (ssz). It was `eth2-testnet-genesis`(protolambda) and `phase0` subcommand? I think we may have some limit to how many empty blocks we'll process but I'm not sure. How would a block you haven't imported have any fork choice weight - you can't process attestations until the block is processed? <dannyryan> Yeah was going to say that the meer existence of attestations is not enough because you need the shuffling. Still though, I suspect each client manages heuristics here. E.g. if I see >50% weight on branch A, then random head from lower depth on branch B is def not the head <dannyryan> A question for geth and el maintainers Do you run the forkchoice and only then execute a new block if it would win the fork choice? If that chain is all VALID, then it sets the head on cl and el But how are we managing B if it's not in the store or protoarray? Or are we expanding optimistic sync to cover every non-canonical fork and then we have to walk back through every block on that fork that's optimistic and call `executePayload` when switching it to canonical (which potentially makes reorg's very expensive)? <dannyryan> In what I am suggesting, I suppose its optimistic but without triggering sync in EL in the normal case because you can walk up the executions on the reory Reorgs on EL are very expensive. Thats what we have to manage appropriately. Otherwise EL must maintain many state tips, which is also presumably expensive but in other ways. Expensive on what is a legitimate reorg signal (enough weight or enough pow in header verification) is at least bound in most cases. Expensive on maintaining and executing N arbitrary tips due to cheap block proposal seems untenable wrt EL state from what I gather Then I suspect we have a problem because importing blocks on the CL side without calling executePayload adds a ton of technical complexity and risk. And then a reorg becomes a hugely expensive event as we have to load and execute every block. I mean I can see the challenge from the EL side if you're using a single-state type approach but it's heading us back towards the original optimistic sync which was way more complex to implement and wound up requiring special handling in a huge range of places in the CL. <dannyryan> The expense of a reorg is bound by the expense of whichever side is more costly. I assume this is EL and that such a reorg in EL would require reexecution in any case It shouldn't need re-execution, just application of state diffs which should be significantly cheaper (no EVM execution) <dannyryan> So this attempts to not have every fork block execute a reorg on EL <dannyryan> 1. Do state diffs exist to be used in this way 2. excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content:
executePayload is not an indication of the chain head - it’s the blocks we need to validate. forkChoiceUpdated is what tells us the head. 
The CL *must* call executePayload on every post-merge block it imports as it’s the only way to validate the block hash.

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: In more normal situations we likely only have one chain head but currently on kintsugi there are a ton of forks are we need to try to follow them all.

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: It would be reasonable for the EL to decide to only sync one of those chains at a time btw (probably best to pick the one forkChoiceUpdated is indicating). The others could check the block hash and return SYNCING and the CL will have to retry it later (or a descendant if there are any).

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: At some point though all those chains likely need to be imported unless finalisation invalidates them first.

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Yeah we need to change how we pick which chain to sync

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: Something in the middle between syncing with everything and with only one chain is to decide to sync with the chain once it's signified by fcU, and still support multiple chain to sync with concurrently

excerpts.author: yperbasis
excerpts.content: Erigon doesn't support multiple chains concurrently. At one point in time there can be only a single current state. A re-org is implemented by reverting state changes from the loser blocks and executing the winner blocks.

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: It does mean that when the head is changed the sync process gets its new target and stops syncing with any other chain, right?

excerpts.author: yperbasis
excerpts.content: The head being ForkchoiceState.headBlockHash, right? We haven't implemented it yet, but that's the idea, yes. To only sync what engine_forkchoiceUpdated tells us and don't sync any other chains.

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: I see, any of these strategies are viable and the final choice is after implementers. Probably, it's really complicated to support multiple syncing processes at a time and doing so doesn't benefit that much. The process of syncing with only a single chain that changes over time should eventually converge despite of the number and frequency of the switching

This sounds like it’s going to be a problem to me. There are multiple chains because forks happen and you need to be able to process blocks on all forks in order to a) validate them and b) process attestations for them which lets you decide which fork is canonical. 
Most forks are only one or two blocks long so Erigon could probably reorg, process the block and reorg back (as long as the json rpc requests in the mean time are delayed so they don’t report from the wrong fork), but during non finality forks can be hundreds of blocks long or more and we still need to be able to process blocks from both sides. Otherwise any network split becomes irreversible.

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content:
What if an EL maintained a map of `block_hash -> execution_payload`. Each executePayload call would push into that map. The map can be pruned based on finality in fcUpdated messages.

Then, the EL can choose to sync based on fcUpdated messages rather than executePayload. The EL will have the full un-finalized tree of payloads, should it get a fcUpdated message that swaps it to another fork. No need for the CL to re-issue payloads.

It means the EL needs to keep the full set of unfinalized payloads around (ram/disk), but that seems like a fairly reasonable requirement to me.
